title: Effects of storage time and temperature on greenhouse gas samples in Exetainer vials with chlorobutyl septa caps
author: Faust, Liebig
materials: Four storage locations differing in ambient temperature were used in the study: laboratory workbench at ambient room temperature, incubator set to 25 °C, walk-in cooler set to 4 °C, and freezer at −10 °C. Storage times were 3, 7, 14, 28, and 84 days. To reduce effects of light, vials for each storage temperature were placed in corrugated cardboard boxes. An Omega SC-GG-K-30-36-PP thermocouple (Omega Engineering, Inc., Stamford, CT) was positioned in each box such that storage temperature measurements could be monitored periodically using a VWR traceable dual laser infrared thermometer (VWR International LLC, Radnor, PA). Mean ± standard deviation temperatures over the 84 day study were 20.4 ± 0.8 °C for room temperature, 23.5 ± 0.4 °C for incubator, 5.2 ± 0.5 °C for walk-in cooler, and −11.3 ± 1.2 °C for freezer (Fig. 1).Fig. 1Storage temperatures over the 84 day study. Storage locations were laboratory workbench at room temperature, incubator set to 25 °C, walk-in cooler set to 4 °C, and freezer at −10 °C. Temperature measurements were obtained using an Omega SC-GG-K-30-36-PP thermocouple (Omega Engineering, Inc., Stamford, CT) positioned in each location using a VWR traceable dual laser infrared thermometer (VWR International LLC, Radnor, PA).Fig. 1

For each storage temperature and time treatment combination, four replicate vials of low and high standards were prepared. After the appropriate storage time had passed, vials were placed on a laboratory workbench and allowed to set at room temperature for 30 min before analysis. At this time, vial temperatures had equilibrated to approximately 21.0 °C as measured by a VWR traceable dual laser infrared thermometer (VWR International LLC, Radnor, PA).

For quality assurance and quality control purposes, each run of samples included hydrocarbon-free air checks every ten samples (n = 5 for each run). Mean (±standard deviation) percent recoveries of expected concentrations for these quality control air checks were 94.4 ± 4.8% for CO2, 103 ± 7% for CH4, and 95.3 ± 8.1% for N2O. Furthermore, six vials each of the low and high standards used in the study were filled the day of each run. Mean (±standard deviation) percent recoveries of expected concentrations for the low standard were 99.3 ± 4.8% for CO2, 98.7 ± 6.0% for CH4, and 109.9 ± 3.4% for N2O. Mean (±standard deviation) percent recoveries of expected concentrations for the high standard were 90.7 ± 6.0% for CO2, 97.9 ± 2.1% for CH4, and 99.6 ± 2.5% for N2O.

steps.title: Prepare storage environment
steps.instruction: Place the Exetainer® vials in corrugated cardboard boxes to limit light exposure. In each box position an Omega SC‑GG‑K‑30‑36‑PP thermocouple (Omega Engineering, Stamford, CT) and monitor temperature periodically with a VWR traceable dual‑laser infrared thermometer (VWR International, Radnor, PA). The four storage locations are: laboratory workbench (ambient room temperature), incubator set to 25 °C, walk‑in cooler set to 4 °C, and freezer set to –10 °C. Mean ± SD temperatures recorded over the 84‑day study were 20.4 ± 0.8 °C (room), 23.5 ± 0.4 °C (incubator), 5.2 ± 0.5 °C (cooler) and –11.3 ± 1.2 °C (freezer).

steps.title: Purge and evacuate vials
steps.instruction: Using Exetainer® vials sealed with chlorobutyl rubber septa (Labco Limited, Lampeter, UK), purge each vial with ultrapure helium (Praxair Distribution, Danbury, CT) for 10 seconds, then evacuate for 15 seconds.

steps.title: Inject gas standards into vials
steps.instruction: Inject 15 mL of a blended gas standard into each prepared vial. Prepare two sets: a “low” concentration standard (certified by NOAA Global Monitoring Division, Boulder, CO on 22 June 2015, certificate CB11245‑A) containing 380 μL L⁻¹ CO₂, 1.790 μL L⁻¹ CH₄ and 313 nL L⁻¹ N₂O; and a “high” concentration standard (certificate CB11061‑A) containing 1000 μL L⁻¹ CO₂, 2.500 μL L⁻¹ CH₄ and 360 nL L⁻¹ N₂O.

steps.title: Store vials for experiment
steps.instruction: Assign vials (four replicates of each low and high standard per treatment) to the four storage locations. Store for the designated durations of 3, 7, 14, 28 or 84 days at the respective temperatures (room ≈20 °C, incubator 25 °C, cooler 4 °C, freezer –10 °C). Keep vials inside the cardboard boxes and continue periodic temperature monitoring with the thermocouples.

steps.title: Equilibrate vials before analysis
steps.instruction: After the assigned storage period, remove vials from their locations, place them on the laboratory workbench and allow them to equilibrate at room temperature for 30 minutes. Vial temperature should reach approximately 21.0 °C as measured with the VWR dual‑laser infrared thermometer.

steps.title: Calibrate gas chromatograph
steps.instruction: Using a Varian CP‑3800 GC equipped with a CombiPAL autosampler and Varian Star Workstation Version 6.41 (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA), run three calibration blends prepared in N₂ (Scott Specialty Gases, Plumsteadville, PA): CO₂ at 350, 424 and 1998 μL L⁻¹; CH₄ at 1.1, 2.08 and 10 μL L⁻¹; N₂O at 82, 411 and 2018 nL L⁻¹. Verify that the coefficient of determination (R²) for each analyte is ≥0.999 before proceeding.

steps.title: Run GC analysis of samples
steps.instruction: Inject each equilibrated vial into the GC and split the sample into two loops: Loop 1 carries 1 mL of sample with ultra‑high‑purity helium (Praxair Distribution, Danbury, CT) to a thermal conductivity detector for CO₂ and a flame ionization detector for CH₄ (hydrocarbon‑free air and ultra‑high‑purity hydrogen provide combustion gas for the FID). Loop 2 carries 0.5 mL of sample with ultra‑high‑purity helium plus a 5 % methane / 95 % argon blend (Praxair) to a ⁶³Ni electron‑capture detector for N₂O. Use the Varian CP‑3800 software to record peak areas and calculate concentrations based on the calibration curves.

steps.title: Perform QA/QC checks
steps.instruction: During each analytical run, insert a hydrocarbon‑free air check every ten samples (n = 5 per run); recorded mean ± SD recoveries are 94.4 ± 4.8 % for CO₂, 103 ± 7 % for CH₄ and 95.3 ± 8.1 % for N₂O. Additionally, each day prepare six vials of the low standard and six vials of the high standard (filled on the day of the run). Mean ± SD recoveries for the low standard are 99.3 ± 4.8 % (CO₂), 98.7 ± 6.0 % (CH₄) and 109.9 ± 3.4 % (N₂O); for the high standard they are 90.7 ± 6.0 % (CO₂), 97.9 ± 2.1 % (CH₄) and 99.6 ± 2.5 % (N₂O).
